newsitem.title: CONGO: Heavy fighting in Congo Brazzaville.
newsitem.headline: Heavy fighting in Congo Brazzaville.

text.p: Heavy fighting raged in the Congolese capital Brazzaville on Sunday between a political militia and troops loyal to President Pascal Lissouba, sending refugees fleeing across the Congo River to Kinshasa.
Western military sources said the "Cobras" -- armed followers of ex-president Denis Sassou Nguesso -- had occupied most of the city centre and surrounded the prime minister's office and treasury.
Refugees reaching Kinshasa said the Brazzaville fighting appeared to be more widespread than in 1993, when 2,000 people were killed in the capital following disputed parliamentary elections.
Brazzaville residents reported a mixture of small arms and heavy machinegun fire.
There was no reliable death toll for the clashes but police sources spoke of several dozen dead and many wounded.
France said it would send 500 troops to reinforce the 450 already there following threats to its nationals and the death of a French soldier on Saturday.
"The Cobras have taken the centre of town and are heading for the town hall. They have captured a number of small armoured vehicles and light tanks from the army," one source said.
Officials at the presidency said discussions had begun with representatives of Sassou Nguesso and other political leaders, but the message had not yet reached the fighters.
But a spokesman for Sassou Nguesso denied that the talks had begun, saying they could not do so until the president's side admitted starting the violence.
Dozens of dugout canoes carrying refugees, mostly small traders originally from Kinshasa, took the "smugglers' route" across the Congo River.
The border has been technically closed on the Kinshasa side since new President Laurent Kabila's forces arrived in the capital of former Zaire, provoking an exodus of Hutus in the other direction.
"French military reinforcements will be flown to Brazzaville beginning tomorrow," said French foreign ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux.
The 450 French soldiers already in Brazzaville were sent in March to evacuate foreigners from Kinshasa if necessary during the final days of the civil war in former Zaire.

One French soldier was killed and five others wounded on Saturday as they tried to evacuate foreign residents from a building where they had been trapped by gunfire. A senior Congolese army officer working with the French soldiers was also wounded.

Doutriaux said about 100 of the 2,200 French nationals in the Brazzaville area had been taken from their homes and regrouped in safe areas because of anti-French sentiment and outbreaks of violence and looting in the capital.
A senior presidency official said a mediation committee had been set up, chaired by Bernard Kolelas, the mayor of Brazzaville and Lissouba's main political opponent.
"We've already got somewhere with the political leaders, but we are having trouble getting the message across on the ground. The thing is now for the soldiers to calm down," he said.
A spokesman for Sassou Nguesso said Kolelas was acceptable as a mediator but that talks could not begin yet.

"Negotiations, even with representatives, have not yet started but we are ready. The aggressor has to recognise that he has committed a serious error before we can go to the negotiating table," Ambrose Noumazalay told Reuters by telephone.
Noumazalay said Sassou Nguesso had no intention of overthrowing Lissouba but was trying to ensure political rights.

"It is not a coup d'etat, it is not a matter of saying we are here or we are there, we simply tried to repulse the aggressors, we haven't attacked, we have only responded," he said, hiswords punctuated by repeated bursts of gunfire.
Fighting began on Thursday after troops surrounded Sassou Nguesso's home to enforce a ban on militias following clashes in the north ahead of July 27 presidential elections.

"The problem is that there are Nguesso's militias and there are Congolese army units which are not under the control of their officers, and so we have seen Congolese troops firing on their fellow soldiers," said Commander Alexis Jaraud, the commander of French forces in Congo Brazzaville.
A plane carrying 44 U.S. citizens across the Congo River from Brazzaville to Kinshasa came under fire on Saturday.
